gloss: The major key with B-flat as its tonic, with the notes B♭, C, D, E♭, F, G, and A, the key signature of which has two flats.
The major chord with a root of B-flat.
The major key with B as its tonic, with the notes B, C♯, D♯, E, F♯, G♯, and A♯, the key signature of which has five sharps.
The major chord with a root of B.
Someone or something that is unbearable and so particularly avoided or disliked; the bane of someone's existence; an object of aversion; an anathema.
byte
A personality type describing people who are relaxed and easygoing and able to engage in leisure activities without worrying about work.
An academic grade, better than a C and worse than an A.
Signifies a second-tier or second class of a given commodity, group, or category, as in B-movie, B-list, etc.
The alternate or secondary part, such as the back side of a phonograph record. Contrasted with ‘A’, which is the primary part.
A low-budget motion picture, especially one with poor production values.
The reverse side of a cassette tape or a phonograph record, especially a vinyl single, often containing songs not considered for airplay.
Any song included on a compact disc single, besides the first song (the A-side).
A simple white sauce made from a roux of butter and flour to which hot milk is added.
An indexed data structure suitable for storage of a large number of items in a balanced fashion, with very few disk accesses required for locating the correct record block.
A type of parametric curve defined by a set of control points, two of which are the ends of the curve, while the others determine its shape.
A city in Hérault department, Occitania, France.
A sauce made of clarified butter emulsified in egg yolks and white wine vinegar and flavored with herbs.
A geographic area and former province in the current Pyrénées-Atlantiques department, Occitania, France.

A former viscounty in the southwestern French Pyrenees, which became part of the French royal domain before it was united with the French crown, together with Navarra, as a single feudal province of the French realm.

the minor chord with a root of B
The note one semitone below B, notated B♭.
A bedbug.
Of or pertaining to Bábism.
A follower of Bábism.

A translator's or interpreter's active language, i.e. in which they are fluent and into which they are able to translate or interpret from their other working languages, but which is not their mother tongue.

The doctrine of a pantheistical religious sect, founded in Persia in 1844 by ʻAlí Muḥammad (1820–1850), who assumed the title of Bábu'd-Dín ("Gate of the Faith"). It combines Muslim, Christian, Jewish, and Parsi elements, and forbids concubinage, polygamy, mendicancy, slave-dealing, and the use of intoxicating liquors and drugs. Precursor to Azalism and Baháʼism.
ʻAlí Muḥammad (1820–1850), the founder of Bábism.
